items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-08-22
items.q: I raised my sister and my brother, that same boy you see Paul there? I paid for his schooling.

ctx.x: And you had to work then?

I raised my sister and my brother, that same boy you see Paul there? I paid for his schooling. Yeah, I paid for his schooling. You see that he went to school? Not me, see that he'd go, but my mother was there, she had him. In fact, none of us was all to get along. He went to school, Paul ought to... Right now, I think Paul got more educated than thinking, gotcha. Don't think he's dumb.

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: Just the same as my oldest brother, Mealy. He's the ringleader of it. He played the fife.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. I didn't think so, you know, because I know you and your brother are both musicians, and I was wondering, did you have other brothers and sisters who were musicians?

Yes, I had one, but he didn't take up an instrument, but he used to play a fife just like I did. Oh really? Yeah. Just the same as my oldest brother, Mealy. He's the ringleader of it. He played the fife. And during those times the fife was very popular around New Orleans. If you don't know what a fife is, it's just a little instrument with six holes in it. Something you would play like a piccolo. It didn't have keys on the side, just three little holes, but you would be surprised the music that we could get out…
Oh that's young. Well how old was your other brother? Was he older than you?

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: Then I and my brothers did work with Thomas. We worked there together. Him on sax and I'm on clown.

ctx.x: And Thomas came and heard Keller's Band and he heard you in the band.

Yeah, I heard me in the band. And that's why Thomas hired me a couple of times. And when I leave Keller's Band, I worked with Thomas. Then I and my brothers did work with Thomas. We worked there together. Him on sax and I'm on clown.
Oh, that was Paul. Paul. He played with Thomas too?

items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: I played with Mealy, Spain and with Abby Williams, George Williams and many others.

ctx.x: Real well then. And then later I'll come to the part where he began to fail. So after leaving Quag, after that job was up, then it was up to 1930. You see I played around with different bands up until 1931. I was playing with Richard Cheaterman in what you call a taxi dancing school they called up there. Then King Oliver came back with the band and asked me to make a trip with him. That was in 1931. Well John Marrero was to go on the trip but he was in bed with the union. He didn't make the trip. So in 1931 we…

Some of this book I believe did you once loan this to Walter Allen? Yeah, I did. And I think he published that in an article, some of it in the record changer. I guess you got that paper that time. Wow. Called the King's Saxophone, remember that article.
